input.question: How far south did Asian contact go, prior to 1606?
input.ground_truth: There was contact between Australian aboriginals and the Torres Strait Islanders, who in turn had contact with the people of Papua, who traded with Western Indonesia, Southeast Asia and beyond. If you travelled, island hopping, from, say, Jakarta to modern Darwin or Perth in 1500 AD, every person you met on the way would have been well aware of their immediate neighbours. However, in the middle of that trek you'd probably have encountered people who were aware of neither Java nor Australia. I think I learned that from Jared Diamond's book *Guns, Germs and Steel* or from one of his other books.
